items.content:
It was an honor to join  @SecWar , Senator Darline Graham, and Governor  @henrymcmaster in renaming Joint Base Charleston in memory of Lindsey Graham.

The names we place on our military installations reflect the service we honor, the character we esteem, and the example we ask future generations to follow. Few Americans embodied those virtues more completely than Lindsey.

He served our nation for 33 years in uniform and more than three decades in the United States Senate, always guided by his belief that the first obligation of government is to keep the American people safe.

Across both of his callings in life, whether the pull of duty brought him to the Air Force or to Congress, a base in Afghanistan or the floor of the Senate, he devoted himself to the same great purpose. He served a cause greater than self.

That is why this base will bear Lindsey's name with pride. And the soldiers who serve beneath it will find in his legacy an example to guide their own.

His name will forever stand as a testament to a life devoted to service, sacrifice, and country. 
Video

— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 10, 2026

items.content:
With President Trump’s policies, the fundamentals for American prosperity are in place because American workers are the best in the world. Today’s jobs report understates the underlying strength of the real economy: Main Street is building, factories are producing, and workers are becoming more productive. July marks the 5th straight month of goods-producing job growth. By creating 105K jobs so far this year, goods-producing employment has had the best 7-month start since 2023. Additionally, productivity growth rose more than double the rate expected in Q2, bolstering the conditions for durable growth and real wage gains for American workers.

Strong Q3 growth expectations further show that the economy is positioned to accelerate. When America produces more and workers become more productive, Main Street wins: higher wages, stronger businesses, more options for customers, and a durable expansion built on inflation-reducing supply-side strength rather than a temporary sugar high.
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 7, 2026

items.content:
A familiar act of mainstream media sophistry: work backward from a partisan verdict and then call the result analysis.

The truth is wages are up for Americans across the distribution, but importantly earnings growth for Main Street workers at the 25th earnings percentile was 5.5% year over year in the latest data this past quarter—more than three times the growth experienced by workers at the 75th percentile. Median weekly earnings also rose a robust 4.6%, well outpacing inflation. This marks a stark improvement from the loss of purchasing power Main Street Americans experienced during the Biden Administration.

Families have not forgotten the pain of Biden-era policies. But President Trump is turning the tide. The fact is, lower-wage workers are leading, median workers are gaining, and the pundit-driven K-shaped economy narrative does not hold up.

BLS has published the wage data for all to see, including journalists willing to look past the haze of their hostility toward the President.
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 6, 2026

items.content:
It was an honor to administer the oath of office to my friend and patriot Jay Clayton as our nation’s ninth Director of National Intelligence in the presence of President Trump, his amazing family and loyal friends in the Oval Office this afternoon.

Jay’s career reflects rare breadth and achievement across law, business and academia. In every role, he has paired the force of his intellect with sound judgment and unquestioned integrity.

As Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Jay modernized oversight of our capital markets while reinforcing investor protection.

As U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, he brought the full weight of American justice to bear against some of the world’s most sophisticated terrorists and criminal networks.

And now, as we approach the twenty-fifth anniversary of September 11th, Jay has again answered the call of public service to ensure our nation discerns danger early, counters it decisively, and never again knows the anguish of that day.

Jay, the President’s confidence in you is well placed.

You will be an outstanding steward of our national security by keeping our country safe and our adversaries ever mindful of America’s vigilance.

So, congratulations to you and your family on this great honor.

I am grateful for your willingness to serve.

I look forward to working alongside you to protect the safety and security of the American people.

And a thank you to Acting Director Bill Pulte for making brave and important choices during his tenure.
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 4, 2026

items.title: The framework for the U.S.-Japan alliance begins with the strong relationship between @POTUS @realDonaldTrump and Prime Minister @takaichi_sanae. We've been in close contact with our Japanese allies, and they are making serious efforts to address the substantial undervaluation of the yen. Through our conversations, we believe they will continue to put the right policies in place to lead the yen’s return to a more normal equilibrium price. Currency intervention is a signal that governments want to change a direction. But only strong, effective policies will result in sustained yen strength.
